title: Integer Moore determinants and iterated Fermat quotients
abstract: Proves Granville's integrality and congruence formulas for iterated Fermat quotients at odd primes, including the exceptional order p - 1. For 1 ≤ d ≤ p and integers x_j prime to p, it proves that the nonzero integer Moore determinant det(x_j^(p^i)) is divisible by p^C(d+1,3), and that the next power does not divide it exactly when the Fermat quotients q_p(x_j) are pairwise distinct modulo p. The development supplies polynomial coefficient identities, denominator-clearing and valuation estimates, a determinant reduction ladder, and weighted Vandermonde formulas over general commutative rings.

informal.GranvilleMoore.exists_intCast_iteratedFe: For an odd prime p, an integer x not divisible by p, any j ≤ p - 1, and any k, the iterated Fermat quotient F^(j)_k(x) is an integer.
informal.GranvilleMoore.dvd_factorial_mul_sub_mul: Under the same prime and unit hypotheses, for j ≤ p - 2 and any k, j! F^(j)_k(x) is congruent to x q_p(x)^j modulo p, where q_p(x) = (x^(p-1) - 1)/p.
informal.GranvilleMoore.dvd_factorial_mul_sub_exc: For an odd prime p and an integer x not divisible by p, (p-1)! F^(p-1)_0(x) is congruent to x q_p(x)^(p-1) - x q_p(x) modulo p.
informal.GranvilleMoore.pow_dvd_det_mooreMatrix: For an odd prime p, 1 ≤ d ≤ p, and integers x_j not divisible by p with nonzero Moore determinant, p^C(d+1,3) divides det(x_j^(p^i)).
informal.GranvilleMoore.not_pow_succ_dvd_det_moor: Under those determinant hypotheses, its p-adic valuation is exactly C(d+1,3) if and only if the integer Fermat quotients q_p(x_j) have pairwise distinct residues modulo p. The Lean statement expresses exactness as failure of divisibility by p^(C(d+1,3)+1).
